answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The comet multiplier is published, charged in juniper, and vertex lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1624 identities would post 4512 proofs and burn roughly 82 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
